title: Improve a small team planning cycle
goal: Explore whether a smaller weekly task list helps a fictional team finish work with less carry-over.

statements.text: The fictional team carried three unfinished tasks into the last weekly review.
statements.source_excerpt: Three tasks remain open at the end of the week.

statements.text: The team selected eight active tasks at the start of that week.
statements.source_excerpt: Eight tasks were marked active on Monday.

statements.text: The team has not yet compared a smaller task list over multiple weeks.
statements.source_excerpt: No repeated comparison has been run.

hypotheses.claim: Reducing the number of active tasks may reduce unfinished work.
hypotheses.rationale: The example shows carry-over alongside a relatively large active list, but one week does not establish a cause.

scenarios.name: Limit active work to five tasks
assumptions: The team can defer lower-priority tasks.
Urgent work does not increase sharply.
scenarios.expected_outcome: May improve focus and expose capacity constraints; some requests will wait longer.

scenarios.name: Keep eight active tasks
assumptions: The team can handle current demand.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Preserves flexibility, but unfinished work may continue if capacity is unchanged.
